newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGBs end Tokyo easier but near day's peaks.
newsitem.headline: Dec JGBs end Tokyo easier but near day's peaks.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tokyo easier on Friday due to corrective selling after sharp gains on Thursday, traders said.
The December ended at 122.10, near the day's peak of 122.12, after recovering most of its losses with the help of small-lot but persistent buying of cash bonds by institutional investors.
It had closed at 122.25 on Thursday.
"Since we're in the historical high levels for JGBs or near uncharted waters, small set-backs are unavoidable if you look at the psychology of the market," said a city bank trader.
Many traders cited the recent introduction of rolling settlements as making dealers wary of short sales.
"Dealers are trying hard to expand holdings of JGBs in order to meet investor purchases for fear of being caught in short positions," said a brokerage trader.
A new rolling settlement system began on Thursday for transactions in JGBs to reduce risks in settlement.
Under the new system, settlement will take place every business day rather than on fixed dates as was the previous practice.
JGB settlement formerly took place on fixed dates -- the 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th and 30th of each month -- and it took from seven to 11 business days to settle JGB transactions.

Furthermore, the recent short-squeeze in the 161st and 163rd JGBs, the cheapest deliverable issues against the September contract, is also making bond participants wary of holding short positions for an extended period, traders said.

Many traders said aggressive short-squeezing of the deliverable issues by U.S. hedge funds pushed some short position holders in the September to the verge of failing to deliver necessary cash JGBs at settlement.
